---
title: "Spada et al. (2011)"
---

> Spada, G., Barletta, V. R., Klemann, V., Riva, R. E. M., Martinec, Z.,
> Gasperini, P., Lund, B., Wolf, D., Vermeersen, L. L. A. and King, M. A.
> (2011). A benchmark study for glacial isostatic adjustment codes.
> *Geophysical Journal International* 185(1), 106-132.
> doi:[10.1111/j.1365-246X.2011.04952.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-246X.2011.04952.x)

Nine codes compared on a spherically symmetric, incompressible, five-layer
earth, with no ocean and no sea level equation. The work was done inside COST
Action ES0701, and Martinec et al. (2018) is its continuation.

The paper divides the work into two classes. Class 1 is the wavenumber
domain: Love numbers, relaxation spectra and the polar motion transfer
function. Class 2 is the spatial domain: surface deformation for an analytic
load. The paper writes a test as "Test X/Y" with Y the class, and the archive
directories are `T01-0X` and `T02-0X`.

```{python}
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

Test 6/1 is the only one that uses a different earth model, the 28-layer
VSS96, chosen because the many layers make the root-finding of the normal
mode method hard.

## What we hold

One archive, `spada2011/spada2011-cost-es0701.tar.gz`, holding 977 files: the
contributor data, 87 GMT plotting scripts, Fortran filter programs and the
PostScript figures. It is a working copy repacked with forty-seven operating
system files removed, which the manifest records.

Eleven README files inside the `T02` directories document the VILMA
submissions: `u` is vertical displacement, `v` horizontal, `e` geoid, in
metres and metres per year, with `*cost` the fine grid and `*costg` the
global grid, both poles omitted.

## Two traps already recorded

Both were found by a G-ADOPT script that reads this archive, and both are
silent.

The `.ela`, `.flu` and `.res` files hold **absolute values** of the residues,
because they exist to make a logarithmic plot. They reconstruct `h` correctly
and get `l` and `k` wrong. The `.dat` files are signed; read those.

The residue lists have **twelve** entries while the relaxation spectrum has
nine. Positions 6, 9 and 12 are Maxwell modes of vanishing strength. Drop
them by fixed position: dropping by magnitude is right at degree 2 and drops
four modes at degree 128, where a real mode is also small.

## Not decoded yet

The 87 GMT scripts in this archive have not been put through
`scripts/decode_gmt_layouts.py`, so the column layouts for the Spada data
files are not written down the way the Martinec ones are. That is the next
piece of work on this collection.
